budgets.name: mem.stream_read_ceiling_gbps
budgets.note: float4 grid-stride read of a 335 MB buffer, 94% of the 1792 GB/s spec peak. A floor on the MEASUREMENT, not a perf claim: it is the reference point every KV-read bandwidth number is divided by, so a broken probe (throttling, wrong device, occupancy collapse) would silently make any ratio fiction.

budgets.name: ornith.router.decode
budgets.note: E=256, H=2048, K=8, seq=1; two-stage dots+select at 128 threads/block. A 64-thread launch was neutral (11.73 vs 11.80 us, E2E unchanged) and was reverted; budget leaves ~19% headroom for clock/occupancy variation.

budgets.name: qwen_moe.router.decode
budgets.note: E=256, H=2048, K=8, seq=1 (frozen Qwen3.5/3.6 decode geometry); narrow strided stage-1 walk + select, warp per row. The instrument: the rejected deep-unrolled uint4 stage-1 walk lands ~30 us (the 31.24 us reading this case was filed under OPEN_TASKS A1), so a regression of that shape is caught here. 1.35x pad over the worst of three observations; the spread was 11.793-11.796 us.

budgets.name: xing.kv_read.decode_gbps
budgets.note: pos-major KV read at ctx 8191: 745 with scalar loads -> 871 after float4-vectorising the score phase (bit-identical). kAttnSplits=4 would reach 1215 but changes the reduction order and was rejected on bit-identity; see the kAttnSplits comment. A REGRESSION guard, not a layout claim: head-major reads faster still in isolation yet makes the decode step slower end to end, so isolated bandwidth does not predict the step.
